methods: Calculated SHA-256 and byte size for all ten supplied PDFs before comparing them with every evidence catalog and prior intake audit.
Reviewed all 83 pages. Seventy-nine pages contained embedded text; GPU-requested OCR recovered readable text from the remaining four pages, with no page requiring manual recovery.
Compared normalized page text and rendered page sequences for the two byte-different duplicate families and retained one established canonical record for each.

Searched every page for delivery dates and times, load volume, hauler identity, manifests, receiving logs, invoices, payments, agreements, rate schedules and cessation evidence before evaluating the receiving-history queue.
Clarified the two generic catalog descriptions whose titles could otherwise misstate the evidentiary value of hauling-related material.

pageIdenticalVariants.basis: Normalized text and the complete six-page rendered sequence are identical to the retained correspondence record.
Normalized text and the complete three-page rendered sequence are identical to the retained March 4, 2019 approval letter.

contentFindings.finding: The 2017 SIU information sheet identifies Wexford County Landfill LLC, permit 590-13, and reports process wastewater averaging 33,000 gallons per day with intermittent discharge.
contentFindings.boundary: The value is an aggregate SIU-profile estimate, not a delivery-level record; the sheet provides no load date/time, actual load gallons, hauler, receiving entry, invoice, agreement or cessation date.

contentFindings.finding: The 2015 pre-inspection report preserves a February 2011 inspection statement that Cadillac's equalization tank accepted hauled waste that was county-landfill leachate.
contentFindings.boundary: The same statement says no flow meter was apparent at that location and supplies no delivery ledger or transaction details.

contentFindings.finding: The June 28, 2019 PFAS status report says Wexford had moved to deep-well injection and had said it would not bring leachate to Cadillac anymore.
contentFindings.boundary: The statement establishes reporting-period cessation context but not the date or details of the final delivery.

contentFindings.finding: The May 2018 email and attached Pace report concern Cadillac biosolids samples and intended land-application fields.
contentFindings.boundary: The email subject 'Hauling' describes outbound biosolids land application, not inbound Wexford leachate loads.

queueDecision: No receiving-history requirement is closed. The batch contains aggregate flow and cessation context but no per-load manifest, receiving log, delivery-linked invoice or ledger, fully executed 2009 agreement and signed rate schedule, signed renewal or amendment, or dated final delivery record.
evidentiaryBoundary: The records corroborate that Cadillac accepted Wexford landfill leachate and later reported that deliveries would stop. They cannot be converted into a load-by-load delivery series or an exact cessation date, and the biosolids hauling correspondence must not be characterized as landfill-leachate transport evidence.
